assessment: The incumbent reliably preserved designs in the observed batch and caught seven fitting problems before dispatch, but required rework and exceeded the time target. Rework clustered in large covers (5/8 versus 2/14 medium and 0/18 small); this supports investigating size-linked fit errors without establishing their cause. Small unadjusted covers taking 25–31 minutes suggest feasible processing times for that subgroup only. The concrete limiting observation is two customer failures on rounded-corner tables: passing the existing reference-table check may not establish customer fit. Wash shrinkage and estimated waste leave further uncertainty; the supplied observations do not establish five-cycle durability or compliance with the area-based waste ceiling.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may create a systematic size-dependent fit error that cutting the whole batch propagates before fitting feedback arrives.
openings.delta: Move fitting feedback ahead of repeated cutting and distinguish an allowance error from cutting or sewing variation.
openings.prediction: If the allowance is responsible, large covers cut and sewn accurately to the current card will show a repeatable directional fit error; transfer or sewing errors instead produce discrepancies between planned and achieved dimensions.
openings.probe: Before bulk cutting, complete one ordered cover per size. Record order dimensions, card dimensions, cut dimensions, finished dimensions, fit and stage working times; also record design, cutting direction and operator. Treat this as a screen, then replicate any suspected error before revising the card. Check revised nesting by area before further cuts.
assumptions: Existing tools permit sufficiently accurate measurements.
Sequencing and measurements fit the three-week window and 350-unit budget; no success-rate or median-time improvement is yet established.

openings.claim: Do customer failures arise from rounded corner geometry independently of actual tabletop dimensions?
openings.delta: Test the reference table's representativeness separately from production accuracy.
openings.prediction: A geometry effect predicts corner-pocket interference on rounded tables despite matching measured length and width; dimension mismatch predicts failure tracking dimensional discrepancy instead.
openings.probe: Ask the six willing customers for actual length, width and corner measurements, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Compare first-placement behavior on measured customer tables and reference tables. Use retained offcuts to screen a removable corner-pocket revision if interference persists; test both-direction dimensional change and the stipulated five-cycle wash performance before adoption.
assumptions: Willing customers include informative table geometries and can report placement consistently.
Any adopted revision honors size and design, uses purchased stock, and passes budget, time, wash and area-waste checks.
